open_points.subject: A28 wall-clock read cardinality across one HTTP request
open_points.text: “the wall clock gives the instant: ... one reading per request” conflicts with “An operation reads the clock once for its own timestamps” and with the exception that “the audit writer takes it when it appends”; one HTTP request can authenticate, authorize, execute a use case and append an audit, each at a different accepted clock-read point.
open_points.question: Does “one reading per request” mean one shared reading for the entire HTTP request, or one reading for each operation/call to system_clock, including the audit writer's separate reading? If it means one shared HTTP-request reading, which module and capability own sampling and distributing that instant, since the flows name none?
options: One wall instant is sampled once per HTTP request and supplied to authentication, authorization, the use case and audit writer.
Each operation calls system_clock.utc_now once, and audit_writer makes its separately permitted call, so one HTTP request may cause several readings.
Business operations share one request instant, but audit_writer still takes a separate instant when appending.
open_points.default_guess: Treat “request” as a call to the clock source: preserve the stated per-operation reads and the audit-writer exception, allowing multiple wall-clock readings during one HTTP request.

witness.initial: A service credential expires at instant T; an import HTTP request enters the transport boundary just before T, and processing reaches service-principal authentication just after T.
events: The producer sends the snapshot import request with that credential.
The transport guard admits the request before T.
service_identity authenticates the credential after T; if admitted, snapshot_import records the attempt and audit_writer appends its audit.
outcomes: With one HTTP-request-wide reading taken by the transport boundary before T, the credential is valid and the import is classified and recorded using the shared instant.
With one reading per operation at each previously accepted point, service_identity reads after T and rejects the credential; no import record or audit is written.
witness.observer: The producer sees success versus 401, and operators see whether an import record and audit exist.
